messages.subject: Saving Intermediate Products
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Is there a way to run ctmm.select in such a way that it saves progress to disk at intervals? It would be nice to be able to pause and resume the execution of longer running functions for various logistical reasons. (For example, one of the HPCs we have access to requires you to split up your job into max 24hr segments. Also, really long running jobs, it would be nice to be resilient against power outages etc.) Is there a way to achieve this?

Best,
Brock

messages.body_plain:
Hello!
I have a series of files (one for each animal) that I need to transform into shapefiles. The method that I have used so far and has worked for 66/79 birds is

sample <- read.csv("data.csv")
#as telemetry
sample <- as.telemetry(sample)
#OUF
m.ouf <- ctmm(sigma=23 %#% "km^2",tau=c(6 %#% "day",1 %#% "hour"))
#set ouf model
ouf<- ctmm.fit(sample,m.ouf)
#do akde
akde <- akde(sample, ouf, weights= TRUE)
#write to frame
shp.frame <- SpatialPolygonsDataFrame.UD(akde,convex=FALSE,level.UD=0.95,level=0.95)
#save
rgdal::writeOGR(est, dsn = ".", layer = "test", driver = "ESRI Shapefile")

However, for 13 birds, this method results in an error message. I have tracked this error to AKDE. For a file that works, the AKDE object that is created with "akde <- akde(sample, ouf, weights= TRUE)" is a "large UD" object with 13 elements. However for these other files (everything else being the exact same about them), the AKDE object created is simply "list of 1" and a warning message of "In akde(sample, ouf, weights = TRUE) :
  Fit object returned. DOF[area] = 3.68581514427619e-17". Why is this happening? I would appreciate input. I can also attach sample files if needed.

Thank you!

messages.subject: Difficultly setting custom bandwidth + Q
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to calculate home ranges using the AKDE function, but am having some difficulty with bandwidth selection.

I have a year of data for 4 vultures, but I have subsampled these datasets so that the mean sampling time is 15 mins. There are, however, still some sampling times slightly shorter than this, and because the akde function takes the minimum sampling time for the bandwidth choice, this leads to home ranges which are difficult to compare and even some ballooning effects where the home range of one bird extends far into the ocean.

Example code:
UD1_pHREML <- akde(birds_as.telem[[1]], FITS_1, weights = TRUE, cores = 0 )
Default grid size of 15 minutes chosen for bandwidth(...,fast=TRUE).
> UD2_pHREML <- akde(birds_as.telem[[2]], FITS_2, weights = TRUE, cores = 0)
Default grid size of 10 minutes chosen for bandwidth(...,fast=TRUE).
> UD3_pHREML <- akde(birds_as.telem[[3]], FITS_3, weights = TRUE, cores = 0)
Default grid size of 5 minutes chosen for bandwidth(...,fast=TRUE).

I have tried to custom set the bandwidth using this command but can't seem to change the grid size selection from minimum:
> UD2_pHREML <- akde(birds_as.telem[[2]], FITS_2, weights = TRUE, cores = 0, grid= list(dr=15))

How should I think about standardizing bandwidth selection so that home ranges are comparable across all 4 birds?

Thanks a lot.

Nick

messages.subject: Re: Difficultly setting custom bandwidth + Q
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

This is unlikely the cause of large range estimates, which are more likely caused by a small effective sample size --- either from the sampling period capturing few range crossings or the movement behavior not being resident. I generally suggest looking at the variogram and an x-y scatter plot colored by time (as in the ctmmlearn workshop scripts).
In either case, the large estimates are likely appropriate and should be equipped with large uncertainty estimates. AKDE is specifically designed to be insensitive to the sampling rate. The sampling rate message is to inform you of the discrete grid used for the FFT, in case the calculation is very slow because of that.

You can include a shape file of the shoreline boundary if the species does not travel there.

There is no situation that I know of where you would want to standardize the bandwidth across datasets. I know that this has been done in the wildlife tracking literature, but I've never seen and cannot think of any statistical justification for this. Instead, use the best estimates and propagate their uncertainties into further calculations.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Overlap issue
messages.body_plain:
Dear Chris,
this mail hopes to find you well.
I am Alessandro, a PhD student. I am working on a dataset on Alpine marmot (Marmota marmota), a medium-sized social rodent. I used 'ctmm' package to estimate the home range of 23 individuals. This worked well and I wrote a manuscript to present my results. Then, peer-reviewers asked me to enrich the study by incorporating information on interindividual variation in space use, along with additional spatial parameters beyond just home range size. They also asked to compare how groups differ between each other. Thus, we would like to do some overlap to compare, for example, how much overlap there is between individuals of the same/different families.
Here, comes the question: I follow the R code present in github but, unfortunately, I am not able to fix the error on my own (code belowe). Do you have any suggetions?

OVERLAP <- overlap(akde(list(all_AKDE),
                        list(all_fit)))

Errore in overlap(akde(list(all_AKDE), list(all_fit))) : list object class not supported by overlap. In aggiunta: Messaggio di avvertimento: In akde(list(all_AKDE), list(all_fit)) : Fit object returned. DOF[area] = 0

> class(all_AKDE[[1]]) [1] "UD" attr(,"package") [1] "ctmm"

I did also the same with a few individuals to see if it may works, but it didn't. (please see the code below).
Prova1 <- overlap(akde(list(Primo_akde[[1]], Rosa_akde[[1]], Checco_akde[[1]], Valentina_akde[[1]], Pigi_akde[[1]], Moana_akde[[1]]), # B2
             list(Primo_fit_phreml, Rosa_fit_phreml, Checco_fit_phreml, Valentina_fit_phreml,
                  Pigi_fit_phreml, Moana_fit_phreml)))

Any suggestion would be appreciated.
Best,
Alessandro

messages.subject: Meta() Forest Plot Customization
messages.body_plain:
Hello group,

I am attempting to improve the readability of the y-axis labels in the forest plots produced by meta(), but I am having some difficulty in doing so. When working with a large number of animals or groups, the labels get extremely small. Attempting to increase the font size with cex, either internally or with a follow-up call to axis(), doesn't seem to work, however. I can change the x-axis tick marks and labels without issue, but when I try to change the y-axis labels, I end up with random numbers pasted over the animal or group labels, instead. Is there an easy remedy to this problem?

Thanks in advance for the help!

Best,
Tyler

messages.subject: trouble importing data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris!

I'm trying to conduct some analyses using the jaguar data from the Jaguar Movement Data dataset, but I'm having trouble importing the data correctly. I've split the dataset, which spans from 1999 to 2016, into separate spreadsheets for each year. My goal is to analyze each year and each individual separately, but I'm unable to import the data at all. I've tried both transforming them into move objects beforehand and importing a CSV file directly, but I always receive some sort of error. For example, when I try to load the attached csv file, it shows the following error in the console:
> length(panthera09) [1] 12 > class(panthera09) [1] "list" > names(panthera09)  [1] "0-357643" "1" "152100" "152150" "152200" "152201" "152351" [8] "152600" "356982" "358447" "497364C" "563517" > panthera09ctmm <- as.telemetry(panthera09) Error in UseMethod("as.telemetry") :  method not applicable for 'as.telemetry' applied to an object of class "list"

You might notice that the names that are returned are not the names of the individuals listed in the table under " individual.local.identifier..ID.", which is another issue I don't know how to resolve.

Honestly, I’ve tried inserting the data in so many ways that I feel like I’m going in circles now. Any clarification you can provide would be immensely helpful.

messages.subject: Re: trouble importing data
messages.body_plain:
Hello Maria,

I do not believe as.telemetry() will work with list objects. Try converting the list into a dataframe or "Move" object first; as.telemetry doesn't have any issues with those two object classes.

Something like this should work:
panthera09 <- as.data.frame(panthera09)
panthera09 <- as.telemetry(panthera09)

as.data.frame has a bunch of options within the function to make sure your columns and rows are transferring properly.

Good luck!

Best,
Tyler
